items.title: Rubio Attacks ICC and International Law at Federalist Society Address

items.summary: A Madras High Court bench of Justices GR Swaminathan and MD Sumathi ruled on November 12 that a community's inclusion in the Other Backward Classes (OBC) list cannot be treated as permanent or automatically justified merely because it has enjoyed reservation benefits for decades. The court said the Tamil Nadu government must demonstrate, to its satisfaction, the constitutional validity of any challenged inclusion or continued retention whenever someone contests classification. Admitting a petition by G Kodeeswaran challenging provisions in the 2016 Government Servants Act granting Backward Class and Most Backward Class status to several Christian communities and converts, the bench found serious doubts over absent objective data on social and educational backwardness and ignored expert commission recommendations. The petitioner argued conversion could grant OBC benefits even to a Brahmin joining the Church of South India, prompting the court to order a serious re-examination of Tamil Nadu's reservation framework.
items.title: Madras High Court Rules OBC Reservation Inclusion Not Permanent or Self-Justifying

items.summary: This morning briefing covers global developments as of Saturday, November 14, 2026. Türkiye and Qatar signed five agreements in Istanbul, including a mutual defense pact ratified by parliament (279-119). The US FAA lifted a nationwide flight ground stop after a telecom outage; officials called it an emergency but not necessarily a cyberattack, with over 10,000 flights delayed or canceled. Trump will meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen at the APEC summit to discuss nuclear weapons reduction. In health news, Nigeria's largest diphtheria outbreak reached 28,151 cases and 1,126 deaths; the US lost its measles elimination status with 5,400 reported cases in 2026.
items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 14, 2026

items.summary: SpaceX launched its reusable Starship rocket from Texas on Friday, aiming for a historic double catch but falling short when the Super Heavy booster splashed down in the Gulf of Mexico amid unknown causes. The upper stage continued orbiting at over 26,000 km/h. SpaceX employees cheered as it sought to advance rapid reusability toward lunar and Mars missions.
items.title: SpaceX Starship Test Falls Short of Double-Catch Goal

items.summary: QR codes have become common for business cards, cashless payments and digital links, but creating one often means dealing with slow websites cluttered by ads, sign-up walls and invasive privacy policies that even hijack your links. A new tool called Ente QR offers a simpler alternative: it is free, requires no sign-ups or usage limits, and comes from The Intelligence's Cool Tools newsletter, which emphasizes protecting user data.
items.title: A Simple, Private QR Code Creator

items.summary: Nearly two months after a 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped at knifepoint in Delhi's Astha Kunj Park on her September 22 birthday, police filed a 450-page chargesheet against three accused—Asif, Hemant and Mukesh—at Saket Court. The survivor alleges she was assaulted twice with weapons while her friend was held; the third man is referred to as Deepu.
items.title: Delhi Gang Rape Chargesheet Filed Against Three Accused

items.summary: Sen. Alan Armstrong of Oklahoma hired T. Lane Wilson, a senior vice president and general counsel at the Williams Companies, as his chief of staff while the latter kept his corporate title during nearly three months in office (April 13 to July 10). The arrangement drew criticism from watchdog groups for creating an obvious conflict of interest, even though Senate ethics rules may not have prohibited it. Wilson held more than $20 million in company stock and continued selling shares worth about $450,000 while serving. Armstrong introduced a pipeline permitting bill that would benefit Williams, which cleared an initial vote. Ethics experts noted the appearance-of-conflict concern remains unresolved.
items.title: Senate Aide's Pipeline Company Ties Raise Ethics Questions

items.summary: On November 14, teenage batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi became the youngest captain in men's T20 history at 15 years and 232 days. Leading Bihar to open the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (SMAT) 2026-27 against Saurashtra at Holkar Stadium, Indore, he had won the toss and elected to bat first. The Bihar Cricket Association named a 17-member squad with Sooryavanshi captain for two matches; Suraj Kashyap was his deputy. He previously served as vice-captain of East Zone under Ishan Kishan in the Duleep Trophy, briefly leading when Kishan left due to injury.
items.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi Becomes Youngest Men's T20 Captain at 15

items.summary: Delhi Police allege a serving Indian Air Force wing commander traded classified military information to a Pakistani intelligence-linked operative in exchange for nude photographs, helping install spyware on five subordinates' devices. Contact ran 21 days (Jan 12–Apr 1, 2026). WhatsApp data shows 3,008 messages and 65 photos exchanged. Leaked details covered a secret drone unit, fighter deployments in Leh, and exercises at Mahajan Field Firing Range.
items.title: IAF Wing Commander Allegedly Traded War Plans for Nudes; Devices Spywared

items.summary: On Friday, the US National Weather Service (NWS) confirmed its radars were operating normally and that its radar website remained fully operational. The agency said outdated content from isolated webpages had been circulating online, but there was no actual radar outage. Previously, its website displayed reports of nationwide internet and communications problems that could have blocked access to products or shown stale information.
items.title: NWS Confirms Radars Operating Normally Amid Rumors of Outage

items.summary: This NVIDIA tutorial serves the quantized, MoE-based GLM-5.3 NVFP4 model (753 billion parameters) locally by tensor-parallelizing it across two GB300-powered DGX Stations over RDMA. It walks through network setup, checkpoint replication and validation, container launch with speculative decoding, and AIPerf benchmarking under concurrency 1 to 32.
items.title: Serving GLM-5.3 Across Two DGX Stations with vLLM

items.summary: Singapore-based billionaire Leo KoGuan vows no further investment in Nvidia without CEO Jensen Huang at its helm, citing his US$1.3 billion (S$1.7 billion) stake and support for the ousted executive amid reports of three affairs. With a $13.2 billion fortune tied to Tesla, KoGuan plans long-term holdings in super-intelligence firms like SpaceX and Alphabet instead.
items.title: KoGuan Halts Nvidia Investment After Jensen Huang's Ouster

items.summary: Microsoft apologized for a global service outage affecting millions of users across at least 70 countries, including Teams, Outlook and Copilot. The company attributed the incident to an earlier network capacity upgrade rather than cyberattacks or AI agents, citing CCTV News. It could not provide a timeline for full restoration and warned of possible intermittent access issues, while public services in Britain's NHS and US federal agencies also reported disruptions.
items.title: Microsoft Apologizes for Global Outage, Rules Out Cyberattack

items.summary: This post shows how to run native Deep Learning Accelerator inference from Python on the Jetson AGX Orin using cuda.bindings.cudla, introduced in cuda-bindings 13.3.0 as a Cython layer over the cuDLA C++ API for hybrid-mode GPU-DLA workflows coordinated through CUDA streams.
items.title: Running Native DLA Inference in Python on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin Using cuDLA

items.summary: Tesla announced a personal-use version of the Cybercab priced at $29,990 with an Autonomy Subscription costing $299 monthly. Elon Musk called the fee too high versus Full Self Driving's roughly $115 per month and said it should be rolled out nationwide after regulatory approval.
items.title: Tesla Prices Cybercab for Personal Use at $29,990 With Autonomy Subscription

items.summary: Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a second employee, according to two people familiar with the matter. The revelation follows two other extramarital affairs that led to his resignation Thursday. Reuters is not naming the second woman and declined comment from Powell, Huang, or Nvidia's board representative.
items.title: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Had Affair With Second Employee

items.summary: On Friday, Tesla announced it is inviting select customers to purchase the Cybercab two-seater with golden butterfly doors for personal use. The vehicle is priced at $29,990 and includes an Autonomy Subscription of $299 per month, which CEO Elon Musk called too high compared to Full Self Driving's roughly $115 monthly fee. Tesla aims to sell robotaxis publicly by year-end after launching unsupervised service in Austin, Dallas, Houston, and Miami.
items.title: Tesla Invites Select Customers to Buy Cybercab for Personal Use

items.summary: Microsoft reported full recovery of Teams, Outlook and other services on Saturday (Nov 14), ending a global outage lasting over 24 hours that crippled email, calendars and virtual meetings for businesses and governments. Reports began climbing around 1725 GMT Thursday; Downdetector logged more than 7.4 million reports worldwide, peaking at nearly 20,000 per minute—over 1,500 times normal levels. The outage hit Exchange Online features specifically and affected regions from Singapore to the United States, delaying earnings for firms including Aviva and Workhorse Group. Analysts noted it was Microsoft's second major disruption this year, deepening concerns about reliance on Big Tech; De Cicco estimated insured losses at US$300–500 million, far below CrowdStrike's 2024 toll.
items.title: Microsoft's Global Outage Ends After More Than 24 Hours

items.summary: OpenAI launched the ChatGPT Wallet, enabling its AI agents to make purchases on users' behalf without exposing card details. Developed with American Express, Mastercard and Visa, it tokenizes payments and requires Face ID or fingerprint approval before each transaction while preserving rewards. Initially rolled out in the United States to ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18+ with eligible US cards, OpenAI plans to expand after gathering feedback.
items.title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Wallet for AI-Agent Payments

items.summary: Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata said he supports the conglomerate's move into new-age businesses such as batteries and semiconductors, while stressing that projects of national importance must be executed with discipline. Speaking at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in New Delhi on Saturday, Noel affirmed his backing for Tata Sons' investments but questioned their delivery. His remarks come amid growing differences with Tata Sons chairman Natarajan Chandrasekaran over three issues: Chandrasekaran's reappointment for another five-year term—passed 4-1 after a deadlock-breaking casting vote by independent director Harish Manwani on 17 September 2026—and opposition to listing Tata Sons, which Noel fears would shift focus from philanthropy to profit. The Trusts collectively own about 66% of Tata Sons.
items.title: Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata Backs Direction but Demands Execution Discipline Amid Group Rift

items.summary: A global outage of Microsoft Outlook and Teams affected 74 countries, renewing concerns about Europe's reliance on a few American tech firms. Amazon, Microsoft and Google together hold roughly 70% of the European cloud market, while European providers account for around 15%, down from about 29% in 2017; Germany's SAP and Deutsche Telekom each hold just 2%. Most EU citizens want European-controlled digital infrastructure, with support highest in Sweden (94%), Finland (93%) and Denmark (92%). On Wednesday, MEPs presented a draft report on the Commission's proposed Cloud and AI Development Act, calling for public authorities to buy more cloud services from European providers. Europe has no single rival to the US giants but has contenders at different layers of the technology stack.
items.title: Europe's Tech Firms Struggle to Replace Amazon, Google and Microsoft After Global Outage

items.summary: Microsoft's November 12, 2026 global outage degraded its services for over 10 hours and hit at least 74 countries, concentrated in the Americas, Europe and Australia. Yet China barely felt it because Microsoft 365 there is run by local provider 21Vianet on an isolated instance, while government agencies migrate to domestic platforms like WPS Office, DingTalk, WeCom and Feishu. This reflects a legal framework built through the Cybersecurity Law, Data Security Law and Personal Information Protection Law that keeps data onshore as sovereign choice rather than default.
items.title: The Microsoft Outage China Barely Felt: A Lesson on Data Sovereignty

items.summary: A Una district consumer disputes redressal commission in Himachal Pradesh ordered a Chandigarh-based shop to refund Rs 29,000 to Mamta Kadyan after her second-hand iPhone 12 stopped working within four days despite a six-month warranty. The ruling also imposed 9% annual interest plus Rs 20,000 for mental harassment and Rs 10,000 toward litigation costs.
items.title: Himachal Consumer Commission Orders Refund and Compensation for Defective Second-Hand iPhone Sale

items.summary: A five-story roundup covers Paytm's RBI digital-wallet license, a Microsoft outage affecting aviation and finance in India (Air India and IndiGo issued updates), IDBI Bank's ₹52,878 crore Fairfax deal, FSSAI dairy-packaging rules, Bharti Airtel's 209% five-year return with debt-free-by-2029 signals, a new RBI transfer facility up to ₹50,000 without bank accounts, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation, and Supreme Court cyber-fraud relief.
items.title: Top Five Indian and Global Tech Stories

items.summary: Microsoft announced that its consumer products and services had fully recovered as of Friday, with the backlog of email messages processed and the issue remediated. The company apologized for a global outage affecting access to email, Teams, and AI assistant Copilot across at least 70 countries. Microsoft attributed the disruption to a technical issue during a network capacity upgrade, unrelated to cyberattacks or AI systems.
items.title: Microsoft Confirms Full Recovery of Consumer Products and Services After Global Outage

items.summary: At an event hosted by lead underwriter JPMorgan Chase, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei pitched the company to investors as one defined by intense AI-safety focus. That emphasis shaped its strategy toward enterprise customers and coding tools rather than consumer chatbots—a path diverging from OpenAI's initial direction. Amid a volatile AI market questioning heavy spending, Amodei emphasized talent and culture, rejecting technically gifted but misaligned hires.
items.title: Anthropic Sells Investors on Safety and 'No Jerks' Culture at IPO Roadshow

items.summary: In an address at UC San Diego, the speaker frames generative AI as a new technological wave echoing Solow's 1987 observation about computers being visible everywhere but absent from productivity statistics. Drawing on historical parallels—basic research preceding practical applications and eventual business reorganization—the talk argues that today we are still in an early adoption phase: surveys suggest 40–50% of workers use AI, with firm-level adoption around 25%, higher (~40%) in knowledge-intensive sectors and lower (~10%) in mining and hospitality. Aggregate labor productivity growth averaged 2.2% from 2020 to 2025, but this began before popular chatbots emerged in 2022, so AI's contribution remains unclear. Task-level gains are substantial for some functions, yet firm-level effects appear modest (e.g., ~1/2 percent boost in sales per employee), likely due to limited scope and offsetting costs. The speaker judges the aggregate productivity impact thus far limited but potentially large over time. Macroeconomically, adoption is raising demand via equity-driven spending and massive data center investment, exerting upward pressure on prices amid supply constraints in memory chips; meanwhile, risks include faster-than-adaptive job displacement and uncertainty about the neutral interest rate r*.
items.title: AI Adoption and Productivity Puzzles in a Macroeconomic Context

items.summary: India's external affairs minister S Jaishankar said at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit 2026 that New Delhi and Washington are in the last stretch of finalizing a highly anticipated trade deal, with most recent changes coming from the American side. He stressed India wants a mutually beneficial agreement that gives it comparative advantage over comparable economies. To catch up on manufacturing missed between the 1960s and 1990s, he cited PLI schemes plus investments in semiconductors, life sciences and AI. Jaishankar also framed 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' as foundational to foreign policy and predicted a more multipolar world order with India playing a stronger role.
items.title: Jaishankar on India-US trade deal's final stretch and manufacturing ambitions

items.summary: In Suzhou, eastern China's Jiangsu Province, emerging technologies are finding practical applications as creative ideas turn into products and traditional industries embrace intelligent manufacturing. The city showcases a range of innovations reshaping everyday life through embodied AI moving beyond the lab—robotic pets, pool-cleaning robots, home service robots and supermarket sorting systems. Precision airbrushes at Galele Innovation Technology bring color and detail to model-making, while Bosideng's smart factory uses robots, AI and automated lines for garment production.
items.title: Inside Suzhou: Where Innovation Comes to Life

items.summary: On Friday, China expressed hope that Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders will adopt a joint declaration at the upcoming 33rd APECEconomic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen from November 18 to 19. Spokesperson Mao Ning noted this marks the first time in 12 years China has hosted the gathering, though it is only the third overall, following Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014. The meeting's theme focuses on openness, innovation, and cooperation.
items.title: China Hopes APEC Leaders Adopt Joint Declaration at Shenzhen Meeting

items.summary: Former CBI special director Rakesh Asthana, who led the Gujarat Police probe into the 2002 Godhra train fire, has rejected a passage in Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's memoir 'Belonging: A Journey of Love' that labels the fire's cause as disputed. Speaking to ANI, Asthana argued the investigation was authentic and upheld by the Nanavati Commission, a Supreme Court-appointed SIT headed by RK Raghavan with CB Satpathy, and the courts. He noted around 44,000 affidavits were submitted before the commission, which examined roughly 1,000 witnesses. Asthana contrasted this with Justice UC Banerjee's committee, which found the fire accidental but was struck down by the Gujarat High Court as illegal.
items.title: Ex-CBI Officer Rejects Sonia Gandhi's Claim That Godhra Fire Was Disputed

items.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar laid out a multi-tier strategy at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in New Delhi, framing Atmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India as building blocks of foreign policy. He noted India missed manufacturing gains during the 'lost decades' (1960s–1990s), with only partial correction via 1991 reforms. Solutions include PLI schemes supporting SMEs, infrastructure upgrades, and scaling semiconductors, AI, bio-life sciences, plus workforce skilling for an AI-driven economy.
items.title: Jaishankar's Blueprint for India Amid Global Fragmentation

items.summary: Senior BJP leader Hardeep Singh Puri resigned his Rajya Sabha seat representing Uttar Pradesh on Saturday, with the resignation accepted by the Chairman effective November 14. He had been elected unopposed to the Upper House last week after two other candidates' nominations were rejected in a Madhya Pradesh by-election triggered by L Murugan's earlier resignation.
items.title: BJP's Hardeep Singh Puri Resigns as Rajya Sabha Member from Uttar Pradesh

items.summary: On Nov. 14, 2026, DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin promoted President Trump's renaming of artificial intelligence (AI) as "SI"—short for "Super Intelligence"—during a national flight ground stop, drawing ridicule on social media. The rebrand traces to July 2025 remarks at the AI Action Plan launch and evolved through polls opened Sept. 19–22 before Trump signed an executive order titled "Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence," directing federal agencies not to acknowledge "AI." Industry figures including Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, and Jensen Huang adopted the term amid concerns it signals U.S. technological dominance over China.
items.title: Trump Administration's Campaign to Rebrand AI as 'Super Intelligence'

items.summary: On the island of Zhaoshu Dao, fishermen Feng Jiahui and Xu Mingwen continue an age-old practice: diving into reefs while holding their breath. This traditional method relies on years of experience passed down through generations. As modern fishing technology advances, this skill is becoming increasingly rare, raising concerns about its future survival.
items.title: Fishing on a Single Breath

items.summary: On the island of Zhaoshu Dao, fishermen Feng Jiahui and Xu Mingwen free-dive six or seven meters into the reefs to catch fish using only one breath and no air tanks. This skill has been passed down through generations via years of practice. Yet fish are becoming harder to find, and fewer young people are choosing to learn this traditional method, raising questions about what happens when the next generation moves on.
items.title: Free-Diving Fishermen on Zhaoshu Dao Face a Vanishing Way of Life

items.summary: CleanTechnica reports Tesla has officially launched sales of the steering-wheel-free Cybercab, with a starting price of $30,000 (technically $29,900). Orders are currently invite-only and require payment of a $1,000 non-refundable deposit. Buyers must also pay an Autonomy fee of $299/month; extrapolated over five years this adds roughly $17,940, bringing the total to about $47,840.
items.title: Tesla Launches Cybercab Sales at $30,000 Starting Price

items.summary: Bharti Airtel founder Sunil Bharti Mittal argued on Thursday that Indian mobile tariffs should rise to about ₹350 per user monthly, citing rising operational costs and a large infrastructure backlog. He noted India has roughly 350,000 towers versus China's over a million, requiring at least doubling capacity plus more fibre and submarine cables. A ₹350 average would still make India the cheapest market globally. Airtel's mobile revenue per user was ₹271 in September, so ₹350 is roughly 29% higher; the last headline hikes came June 2024 with only three increases since 2019. Analysts had expected a round after Jio's listing.
items.title: Sunil Mittal Advocates Indian Mobile Tariff Hikes Amid Rising Costs and Infrastructure Gaps

items.summary: AI is reshaping publishing in a chaotic, unregulated way. Romance novelist Coral Hart uses it to write 370 novels under 21 pen names since 2025, earning high six figures by selling per page on Kindle Unlimited. A peer-reviewed study led by Tuhin Chakrabarty estimates around one fifth of recently self-published books contain at least 25% AI-generated text. The backlash is fierce: users face doxxing and death threats when disclosing use, while publishers like Hachette have cancelled deals over suspicions. Writers accuse large language models of training on stolen work, prompting lawsuits against Anthropic for a $1.5bn settlement involving around 500,000 titles. Detection tools like Pangram claim near-95% accuracy, yet accusations disproportionately target authors of colour and non-native speakers. Experts call for clearer policies and transparency as the industry grapples with copyright gaps and shifting creative norms.
items.title: 'It's like the wild west': how AI has rocked the literary world

items.summary: Former England captain Millie Bright helped distribute new football kits to grassroots teams in Leeds through anti-discrimination charity Kick it Out, which selected thirty teams from communities facing social or economic challenges. The initiative, funded by the Morrisons Foundation and supported by Champions CIC founder Craig Gilmore, addresses kit costs as a barrier keeping girls engaged in sport.
items.title: Football Kit Giveaway Aims to Boost Participation

items.summary: One tout advertises up to £1m of U2's 2027 tour tickets via StubHub, prompting scrutiny. Vladyslav Skrypka alone lists more than 2,000 tickets at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, some priced above four times face value for a potential over-£1m profit. The case intensifies calls on Lisa Nandy to advance legislation banning resale-for-profit and bot use before the parliamentary session ends in 2027.
items.title: U2 tout listings on StubHub fuel debate over ticket resale clampdown

items.summary: A Guardian investigation found hundreds of children in England received prescriptions for weight-loss GLP-1 medications, including some under 12. In the financial year 2025-26 there were 419 prescriptions to children under 18 (10 younger than 12), and over April-July this year, 341 prescriptions (15 for those under 12). Figures from the NHS Business Services Authority likely underestimate totals as they exclude private, prison and hospital use. This rise coincides with increasing childhood obesity: 10.7% of reception-year children are obese versus 22.8% in year 6. Experts stress these drugs suit only specialist cases and require long-term lifestyle support.
items.title: Rising Prescriptions of Weight-Loss GLP-1 Medications for Children in England

items.summary: After a security breach linked to North Korea stole $6.3 billion last month, Binance said it aims to reopen withdrawals for all remaining networks and assets by the end of next week; 87 networks were reopened this week after covering 95% of stolen tokens in what experts call the largest crypto theft ever. The FBI blames Pyongyang, which denies involvement.
items.title: Binance Aims to Reopen Withdrawals After North Korea–Linked $6.3 Billion Hack

items.summary: IOM and UNHCR warn that funding shortfalls have depleted emergency shelter supplies for Sudan, where $2.9 billion (€2.62bn) is needed to reach 20.4 million people but only 47% has been raised. Of the 33.7 million dependent on aid, just 15.4 million need basic household goods yet only 10% have received help. Experts Marina Peter and Ivo Körner condemn donors—especially Germany and the EU—for sharply cutting contributions. The UK-led October statement covering 19.5 million people (41% of the population) faces criticism from Khartoum, which denies famine warnings. Between 40,000 and 250,000 have died since the war began three years ago.
items.title: Sudan's Humanitarian Crisis Deepens as Aid Funding Collapses

items.summary: The European Commission has agreed a breakthrough allowing Eurotunnel to trial airport-style border controls at Folkestone and Calais. Owner Getlink's chief executive Yann Leriche will present a 40-page proposal for drive-through terminals using eagle-eye cameras, biometric kiosks and police monitoring—inspired by US-Mexico, Rome and Paris airports—to prevent short- and long-term chaos while the delayed Entry/Exit System (EES) remains unresolved. The two-year trial could become permanent.
items.title: Eurotunnel Trials Airport-Style Eagle-Eye Border Checks Under UK-EU Breakthrough

items.summary: With under two months until the polls, incumbent President Bola Tinubu faces former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and opposition figure Peter Obi. Concerns mount that INEC's preliminary voter register contains images possibly generated by artificial intelligence—showing exaggerated facial features and inconsistencies like duplicate names or deceased individuals. This raises questions about electoral preparedness ahead of the 2027 general elections, amid broader continental worries over AI in voting. Nigeria has already dealt with fabricated media before; deepfakes falsely linking candidates to terrorism circulated during the 2023 election. Experts warn that beyond influencing voters through inflated crowds, a deeper danger lies in people doubting authentic information once they know convincing fakes exist.
items.title: How AI Disinformation Threatens Nigeria's 2027 Elections

items.summary: The White House announced that President Donald Trump will meet Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping next week. The trilateral meeting is scheduled to take place in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Leaders' Meeting. Trump plans to discuss nuclear weapons reduction, but not Ukraine.
items.title: Trump, Xi and Putin Set for Trilateral Meeting in Shenzhen at APEC

items.summary: Ramachandra Guha revisits Walter Crocker's Nehru: A Contemporary's Estimate, first published in 1966 and now six decades old. Writing on Jawaharlal Nehru's 137th birth anniversary, Guha argues the book is both little known and timely. Crocker, an Oxford-trained Australian who served as high commissioner to New Delhi for two spells of roughly three years each from the mid-1950s onward, offers a judicious assessment of Nehru the statesman—praising his holding together of India amid religious rivalry, poverty and illiteracy—and admiringly portrays him as an unusually charismatic man. Guha notes one weakness: Crocker underappreciates Gandhi's influence on Nehru.
items.title: Walter Crocker's Nehru Remains Essential Reading Six Decades Later

items.summary: Researchers in China investigated screen-printing-induced degradation in copper-plated silicon heterojunction (HJT) solar cells, a concern as the industry seeks cheaper alternatives to silver. They found conversion efficiency declined from 26.2% to 25.7% over 15,000 printing cycles, driven by reduced open-circuit voltage and fill factor. Confocal microscopy showed mesh knuckle wear increased contact with wafers; minority carrier lifetime degradation rose from 0.61% new to 11.0% after cycling. An emulsion buffer layer mitigated damage: a 4.7% coverage ratio limited lifetime degradation to 0.41% over 10,000 cycles while preserving coating uniformity. Published in Solar Energy, the work arrives amid rising interest in copper metallization, with Nankai University reporting a silver-free HJT cell at 25.2% and Forschungszentrum Jülich achieving 23.08% in fully copper-metallized cells.
items.title: Mitigating Screen-Printing Degradation in Copper-Plated Heterojunction Solar Cells

items.summary: Defending WBBL champions the Hobart Hurricanes suffered their sixth straight loss, dismissed for just 88 inside 18 overs. Brisbane Heat chased down the total in only 5.4 overs to win by 10 wickets. Grace Harris top-scored with an unbeaten 52 off 22 balls.
items.title: Brisbane Heat Rout Hobart Hurricanes by 10 Wickets in WBBL Final

items.summary: CATL's Tener Sodium battery energy storage system (BESS) is a sodium-ion product positioned against lithium-ion offerings, launched at The Smarter E event in Munich. Presented by CATL product solution manager David Santiago on an ATA Insights webinar, the four-hour system uses paired cabinets—two to eight per block—and delivers over 30 MWh with up to 7.5 MW output and 95% round-trip efficiency. CATL claims sodium cells generate substantially less heat than its EnerX LFP system, reducing DC refrigeration needs for a 50 MWh station from 720 kW to 490 kW. For a 500 MWh project, the sodium layout uses fewer blocks and roughly 32% less footprint, with estimated EPC cost savings around 9.2%. Overseas delivery is targeted for summer 2027.
items.title: CATL Tener Sodium BESS specifications and competitive positioning

items.summary: This article previews six new fiction novels arriving in the festive season, all information sourced from publishers. Rachid Benzine's The Man Who Read Books follows a Gaza ceasefire photographer who discovers an old bookseller sharing literature that helped him survive exile and imprisonment. Saba Brelvi's The Squatters sees Dalia Waheed help pregnant Hajira find housing amid political danger in Surrey near London, UK. Stephane Wrobel's Revenge Plot features Arnie Tenderton targeting literary agent Claudia during Christmas in the Catskills mountains. Dana Renee Green's Every Goodbye Ain't Gone portrays Renie, a 39-year-old mother of seven diagnosed with Stage 4 breast cancer given three months to live, who begins journaling for her children and decides to live on her own terms. From Premee Mohamed and Jonathan Sims, The Library of Jurgen Leitner offers two parallel stories of employees drawn into deadly books in an eerie private library.
items.title: Six New November Fiction Novels for Festive Reading

items.summary: The Indian market rebounded sharply in early November, led by largecaps. Among ten top performers, six delivered multibagger returns over three to five years: Shriram Finance (147% at 3y/199% at 5y), Muthoot Finance (120%/68%), Mahindra & Mahindra (116%/255%), Ashok Leyland (95%/132%), HDFC AMC (91%/99%) and Divi's Laboratories (226%/136%). Bajaj Finance, Lodha Developers, Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Company and HDFC Bank posted strong November gains but lagged in the long run. The article is written by an unregistered author with no financial interest.
items.title: Six of Ten Top November Largecaps Were Multibaggers in the Long Run

items.summary: A viral clip showing Odisha BJP MLA Manoranjan Dyan Samantara making a biting gesture near his ear during an interview with Fisheries Minister Gokulananda Mallik has sparked controversy. His wife, Meena Sahu, claims the footage was AI-generated to malign him and blames opposition BJD's Chikiti social media team. The authenticity of both videos remains unverified.
items.title: Odisha BJP MLA's Viral 'Ear-Biting' Clip Disputed as AI-Generated by Wife

items.summary: A dispute emerged between Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu after Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu's remarks at a partnership summit. A Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam spokesperson claimed Naidu underestimated Tamil Nadu's investment appeal, sparking tension. Reports clarified his comments targeted reporters rather than the state, especially since he had praised southern states' cooperation.
items.title: Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu Clash Over Industrial Investment Comments at Partnership Summit

items.summary: Physicist Steven Koonin, a senior fellow at Stanford's Hoover Institution and former Obama energy department official, argued at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit that India should secure its energy needs first and defer decarbonisation until it is richer. Speaking as COP31 convenes in Antalya, Türkiye through November 20, he said global emissions are soaring while promised climate finance has not materialised. Koonin dismissed the present climate emergency, citing long-term Indian records showing no support for such a crisis, though he conceded humans influence warming and called nuclear energy essential to India's future—aiming to raise capacity from about 8.8 GW to 100 GW by 2047.
items.title: Steven Koonin Urges India to Prioritise Energy Before Decarbonisation at HT Leadership Summit

items.summary: Government-aligned Giants Brigades claim they repelled a Houthi attack in Lahj province, posting footage of fighters fleeing. State media reported airstrikes on Houthi reinforcements in Taiz and the seizure of drone components bound for Houthis. The International Organization for Migration says military escalation has displaced more than 340,000 people since August, worsening Yemen's humanitarian crisis amid Operation Dawn of Yemen.
items.title: Yemen's Government Forces Repel Houthi Attack as Displacement Mounts

items.summary: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh invoked Prime Minister Narendra Modi's "abki baar, AQI 400-paar" slogan from the 2024 election campaign to criticize worsening air pollution in New Delhi. He claimed Delhi had become the world's most polluted city, with breathing growing difficult and hospital patients rising as multiple monitoring stations recorded severe (400-500) AQI levels for days.
items.title: Congress Mocks Modi Over Delhi AQI Crossing 400 Amid Pollution Crisis

items.summary: The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), running in Goa from November 20 to 28, has drawn criticism for its Indian Panorama line-up. Veteran filmmaker Adoor Gopalakrishnan said the Centre is 'not interested in films with artistic merit' and expects similar treatment at the National Film Awards. His film Padayatra was omitted despite his stature; he called it a continuation of marginalising quality cinema.
items.title: IFFI 2026 Indian Panorama Snubs Adoor Gopalakrishnan's Padayatra Amid Ideology Debate

items.summary: In a pulsating AFLW semifinal at Kardinia Park, Sydney beat Geelong 8.2 (50) to 7.5 (47), advancing to its first-ever preliminary final and setting up a clash with two-time premiers North Melbourne. The game drew concern as ruck Piper Dunlop was stretchered off after a head clash; Geelong also lost Amy McDonald, Rachel Kearns and Georgie Prespakis to injury.
items.title: Sydney Swans Reach Maiden AFLW Preliminary Final Past Geelong in Close Semifinal

items.summary: Over the past five years, Indian markets have swung sharply amid AI-driven volatility and Middle East tensions. While benchmark indices like Nifty 50 (around 39%) and Sensex (34%) delivered modest gains, a handful of stocks became 'tenbaggers,' with Cupid leading at roughly 16,413% over five years—rising from Rs 2.33 to around Rs 385 per share. The article draws on Peter Lynch's investing philosophy: buy what you know and love, focus on overlooked gems rather than chasing hot trades, and stay disciplined amid volatility. Lynch reportedly bought more than a hundred tenbaggers during his time managing Magellan, including Ford Motor and General Electric.
items.title: Tenbaggers on Dalal Street: Peter Lynch's Rules for Finding India's Next Big Winners

items.summary: Japan coach Eddie Jones returns to Twickenham, promising his youthful side will attempt a major upset against England. Having lost all six previous tests versus England and suffering a narrow 28-21 defeat to Wales in November's Nations Championship opener, Japan seeks revenge after the Brave Blossoms famously beat South Africa at the 2015 World Cup under Jones.
items.title: Eddie Jones Vows Japan Will 'Play the House Down' Against England

items.summary: Citizens in South Sudan began registering on Saturday for the country's first general elections since independence from Sudan in 2011. Originally set for December, voting dates are uncertain amid concerns about readiness given ongoing violence and political tensions. Former vice-president Riek Machar remains under house arrest while President Salva Kiir leads; a civil war between their forces killed more than 400,000 people.
items.title: South Sudanese Begin Registering Ahead of First National Elections

items.summary: The US has assured India a comparative tariff advantage for its merchandise once Section 301 investigations conclude, marking a breakthrough in bilateral trade talks. Two probes launched in March—one on forced labour and another covering 60 economies including India—will shape final tariffs. Indian exports to the US grew from $51.99 billion to $59.52 billion over April–October of FY2026-27, underscoring Washington's status as New Delhi's largest export market.
items.title: US Assures India of Comparative Tariff Advantage Amid Bilateral Trade Talks

items.summary: David Garza, chief executive of the educational group Tecmilenio since 2020 that houses Mexico's prestigious private university Tecnológico de Monterrey along with its continuing education and health research divisions, outlines a strategy centered on applied research, talent development, and entrepreneurship. The institution operates in 40 Mexican cities and aims to boost these areas amid AI-driven disruption. Garza notes more than 50% of professors have received training, reflecting intensive classroom use of artificial intelligence since ChatGPT emerged rather than banning it. Nearly 20% of recent graduates take up entrepreneurship as their first job. The university also holds the world's largest biobank of genetic information for a Hispanic population segment with 100,000 samples.
items.title: David Garza on Tecnológico de Monterrey's AI-Era Strategy

items.summary: Economist Branko Milanovic (73), a former World Bank senior economist now at CUNY, discusses the U.S. midterm results three days after his EL PAÍS interview. He argues Trump's defeat will not significantly alter US policy toward China, the Middle East or Europe, noting that even Joe Biden did not change these policies and that money does not guarantee electoral success for tech billionaires like Elon Musk. Milanovic introduces 'homoploutia' to describe a new elite combining high capital and labor income. He attributes globalization's crisis to a paradox: neoliberalism reduced inequality but empowered China at American hegemony's expense, fueling inter-nation conflict and middle-class impoverishment in developed nations.
items.title: Branko Milanovic on Trump's Defeat and Global Inequality

items.summary: A nationwide ground stop halted US flights for hours due to air traffic control communications issues, which the FAA described as safety and communication problems. Travellers across the country were affected before flights were permitted to take off again.
items.title: US Flights Resume After Nationwide Ground Stop

items.summary: Mumbai captain Suryakumar Yadav silenced selection criticism with a 15-ball fifty and blistering 60 off 21 deliveries, guiding Mumbai to a seven-wicket win chasing just 173 in their Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy opener against Hyderabad. His six boundaries and five sixes earned him player of the match as he pursues a return from India's T20I squad.
items.title: Suryakumar Yadav's Rapid Firepower Defuses Selection Doubts After India Snub

items.summary: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma will visit the site of a deadly road accident near Kaziranga on Saturday morning to meet affected families. The head-on collision between a passenger mini-bus and a container truck at Rongajan in Golaghat district killed 26 people, with around 20 others injured. Many victims were students returning from classes.
items.title: Assam CM Himanta Sarma To Meet Families After Kaziranga Accident Claims 26 Lives

items.summary: SpaceX aborted its attempt to catch the Super Heavy booster with tower arms, diverting it to the ocean after a Friday 16:45 local launch from Boca Chica, Texas. The upper Ship stage continues deploying 26 Starlink satellites and will complete 14 orbits before returning in 22.5 hours for a possible second catch at about 15:15 Saturday. This is the company's first full-recovery attempt toward making Starship reusable; SpaceX previously caught the booster three times but never grabbed the upper stage. Prof Malcolm Macdonald of the Royal Aeronautical Society noted full reusability could change space economics, though one flight won't prove it.
items.title: Setback for SpaceX Starship rocket's double-catch test

items.summary: A Class 9 student in Guwahati allegedly stabbed his mother, Chandrani Kalita, with a sharp weapon at their home in Jyotinagar on Friday. She was rushed to Gauhati Medical College and Hospital (GMCH) and remains critically injured in the ICU. The boy later died after reportedly falling from a building in the city's ABC area.
items.title: Assam Student Stabs Mother Then Dies After Building Fall

items.summary: Vercel Labs released Vercel UI SDK, an open-source beta library of interface behaviors built for coding agents rather than finished components. The headless library ships 50+ behaviors and 51 component modules across six npm packages at version 0. 1. 0-beta. 1 under Apache-2. 0, published November 12, 2026. Agents assemble primitives defined with definePrimitive into framework-specific parts via createParts in React 19+, Vue 3. 5+, Svelte 5. 33+ and Solid 2 RC adapters. Behaviors span focus, selection, popups, drag-and-drop and virtualization across ten categories; prebuilt components include Select, Combobox and Menu. Agents learn the library through a skill prompt added to AGENTS. md or llms. txt, while createAgent() lets them operate UI state directly via snapshot and act methods without screenshots.
items.title: Vercel Releases UI SDK for AI Coding Agents

items.summary: Congress party's overseas leader Sam Pitroda addressed scrutiny over his exchange of Diwali and New Year greetings with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. In an NDTV interview, he said the gesture was personal, that he can separate personal relations from political rivalries, and that his own relationship with Modi differs from Congress's attacks on him. He denied ideological alignment, saying his idea of India does not prioritize religion in politics, while noting he could still disagree yet share coffee.
items.title: Sam Pitroda Separates Personal Bond With Modi From Political Rivalry Amid Congress Attacks

items.summary: The FAA lifted a rare nationwide ground stop on Friday that had grounded more than 14,500 flights for over four hours after an outage in the US air communications system. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed aging, overloaded equipment and ruled out terrorism or cyberattack. Airline shares fell—American dropped more than 2% and United 1.6%. This is only the third such order ever issued, previously on Sept. 11, 2001 and in January 2023. Duffy blamed Congress for withholding repair funds and urged approval of $50 billion to upgrade infrastructure through an emergency bill.
items.title: FAA Lifts Rare Nationwide Ground Stop After Air Communications Outage

items.summary: On Nov 13, Tesla announced it is inviting select customers to buy the two-seater Cybercab robotaxi for personal use. Priced at US$29,990 (S$38,660) with an Autonomy Subscription of US$299 a month, CEO Elon Musk said sales would begin across the US upon regulatory approval and aim to reach customers by end of 2026.
items.title: Tesla Invites Select Customers to Buy Cybercab Robotaxi for Personal Use

items.summary: Microsoft said its services were fully restored after a major outage that disrupted governments, businesses and public services worldwide. The incident began Thursday around midday in the US and 6pm UK, affecting courts, healthcare, airlines and banks across Japan, Singapore, Australia, the UK, France, Belgium, the Netherlands and Taiwan. In the UK, NHS England staff used paper records while ambulance services reported a serious impact; US House staffers lost a day of work. Microsoft said approximately 430 million people use its apps and cited more than 70 countries reporting problems via Downdetector. The company apologised Friday, saying the outage was not cyber or AI-related but stemmed from an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade.
items.title: Microsoft Restores Services After Global Outage Hits Governments and Businesses

items.summary: Microsoft said Saturday that services were fully restored after a massive outage lasting hours, affecting Microsoft 365 apps including Outlook, Teams and Copilot. Downdetector received reports from more than 70 countries within an hour of problems emerging midday Thursday in the US. The disruption hit governments—Japan, Singapore, Australia—and reached courts, healthcare services, airlines and banks worldwide; Britain halted a Manchester trial while police urged people to phone in urgent requests. Over 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, and the company reported more than 450 million paid commercial subscriptions as of January. Microsoft apologised Friday, stating the outage was not cyber-related or caused by AI agents but stemmed from an issue during a network capacity upgrade following a recent change.
items.title: Microsoft Restores Services After Hours-Long Global Outage

items.summary: Tesla posted the agreement for its $29,990 two-seat Cybercab: it cannot operate without a mandatory $299 monthly Autonomy Subscription that Tesla can reprice with one month's notice, suspend for up to a week after three 'strikeouts,' or cut off entirely. The car has no steering wheel or pedals and works only inside Robotaxi geofences whose coverage the article found was 59%–78% of advertised maps. Over five years, the vehicle plus 59 paid months totals $47,631 before insurance, registration, charging and taxes. The author argues this is unfair because Model Y owners already run identical AI4 hardware and software in the same geofences yet pay only a $99/month supervised FSD fee; Tesla began selling that package in 2016 for up to $15,000 before moving to subscription in February. The piece frames the Cybercab as effectively an endless variable-rate lease with a large down payment.
items.title: Tesla Cybercab's mandatory $299/month autonomy subscription and its contrast with Model Y FSD owners

items.summary: A 24-year-old founder of the AI startup Lycana has become entangled in Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital scandal because he shares the same name. Until recently, he viewed the association as a professional advantage: interviewers greeted him with 'Oh yeah, you're the Nvidia CEO,' and recruiters jokingly asked if he had extra GPUs. That perception shifted after reports surfaced about Huang's affairs, including one involving a woman accused of spying for China. The founder said his admiration diminished, arguing that professional success should not shield personal misconduct. He initially posted humorous content on LinkedIn but worried unfamiliar people would mistake him for the CEO as discussions spread across Reddit and RedNote.
items.title: AI Founder Dragged Into Jensen Huang Scandal Over Shared Name

items.summary: On Friday the 13th, November 2026, a major Microsoft outage halted digital communication for millions worldwide and disrupted public services including hospitals and schools. While its exact cause remains unclear, the event underscores risks from market concentration as cloud computing centralizes essential infrastructure among few corporations—Microsoft itself once framed this dominance as strength. The incident is not isolated: July 2024 saw a faulty Windows update crash systems affecting pharmacies, airports and banks; October 22 revealed vulnerabilities in software underpinning roughly 70 per cent of the world's websites; and OpenAI agents reportedly hacked government infrastructure months earlier. An anthropologist studying data centres notes that understaffing compromises testing capacity, while sociologists warn growing dependence on interconnected systems amplifies failure consequences.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Highlights Fragility of Concentrated Digital Infrastructure

items.summary: Reuters reports that Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang allegedly misled senior executives about his personal relationship with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang. The report, based on internal October communications and two sources familiar with the matter, names general counsel Tim Teter and marketing officer Alison Wagonfeld among those told misleading information. Huang resigned as CEO, president and board member on November 12 following reports of extramarital relationships including one with Huang. A separate claim suggests U.S. intelligence agencies suspected her Chinese ties, though this remains unverified.
items.title: Jensen Huang Controversy Unfolds After Resignation

items.summary: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet on November 13 in partnership with American Express, Mastercard, and Visa, enabling its Dots AI agents to find products and prepare online checkouts for user approval. Available only to US-based ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18+ using eligible credit cards, the tool uses tokenization so retailers never see real card details while preserving rewards and dispute protections. Users must biometrically authorize each purchase; OpenAI plans future guardrails like spending caps.
items.title: Explained: How does OpenAI's newly launched ChatGPT Wallet work?

items.summary: Microsoft said Saturday that a more than 24-hour global outage affecting its Microsoft 365 applications has ended, beginning around 1725 UTC Thursday. Teams, Outlook and Copilot were hit, disrupting businesses and governments worldwide with over 7.4 million reported problems. Germany's federal ministry noted significant business impact while health functions continued; Britain's NHS fell back on paper records. Microsoft blamed server issues, not outside interference.
items.title: Microsoft Says All Services Working Again After Global Outage Ends

items.summary: Google launched its first Gemini AI smart glasses, priced at $395 (about ₹35,000), with sales beginning December 10 in the US and South Korea. The device features a 12MP camera, 9-hour battery life, live translation across 70+ languages, and privacy safeguards like face-blurring and recording-light detection—positioning itself against Meta's Ray-Ban glasses.
items.title: Google Unveils Gemini AI Smart Glasses; Challenges Meta's Market Dominance

items.summary: Colette Kress, Nvidia's finance veteran of 13 years, now serves as interim CEO after challenging co-founder Jensen Huang. A Wall Street Journal report describes an August confrontation where Huang called her a 'deer in the headlights.' Their dispute centered on billions in financial guarantees to AI companies unable to afford Nvidia chips, including a scaled-back OpenAI Ohio commitment from USD 250 billion to under USD 120 billion.
items.title: Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress's Israel link and how she challenged Jensen Huang

items.summary: Microsoft reported on Saturday that services had fully recovered across Teams, Outlook and its other products, ending a global outage lasting over 24 hours. The incident disrupted essential functions such as sending emails, managing calendars and hosting virtual meetings for businesses and governments worldwide. Microsoft attributed the problem to server issues affecting Copilot AI assistant but ruled out malicious activity or AI as the cause.
items.title: Microsoft Restores Services After Global Outage

items.summary: Following a Microsoft 365 service disruption on November 12, the company warned users that cybercriminals are exploiting the outage to send phishing emails impersonating official service health notifications. Some messages falsely claim held emails will be deleted within 24 hours unless recipients click links. Microsoft urged organizations to verify alerts through the admin center and investigate suspicious activity.
items.title: Microsoft Warns Outlook and Teams Users Against Fake Outage Emails

items.summary: US media report that Singapore confiscated the passport of Alice Huang, former chief executive of Megaspeed, in June 2025 and restricted her from leaving the country for eight months. Authorities investigated whether she collaborated with California-based Supermicro to export servers containing advanced Nvidia chips to China amid espionage questions tied to Jensen Huang's affair. US officials were reportedly unresponsive; Singapore sought help from the Justice Department and FBI but received little support.
items.title: Singapore held Alice Huang’s passport for months but got little US assistance in Nvidia chip investigation: Report

items.summary: In Guwahati, Assam, Class 12 student Arunabh Kalita allegedly stabbed his mother Chandrani at their Jyotinagar home before jumping to his death from the 10th floor of Mayur Heights. After he sent alarming WhatsApp messages, Principal Chanmari Police responded; she was rushed to GMCH where her Glasgow Coma Scale improved from 9/15 to 15/15, though prolonged treatment remains needed.
items.title: Guwahati Student Stabs Mother Before Jumping From High-Rise; She Recovers

items.summary: A long-time Apple TV owner praises its ease of use and interface, which beat Roku, Amazon, and Google streamers. Yet the November 13, 2026 model disappoints: excellent hardware but flawed software in tvOS 27, plus a price double that of the still-working 2022 version. The reviewer will skip this generation until Apple fixes its weak TV app.
items.title: Why to Wait on the New Apple TV 4K (2026)

items.summary: After a security breach linked to North Korea stole US$6.3 billion (S$8.1 billion) in October, Binance aims to reopen withdrawals for all remaining networks and assets by the end of next week. It had already reopened 87 networks this week and covered 95% of stolen tokens. The FBI and Binance blame Pyongyang, which denies involvement; a North Korean group called TraderTraitor is also implicated.
items.title: Binance targets full reopening of withdrawals by next week

items.summary: Elon Musk joined a petition, now signed by over 43,000 people, to reinstate Jensen Huang. The open letter on Stand with Jensen asks the board to restore Huang or give an evidence-based reason for his removal, demand an independent investigation and provide public explanation of its concerns. Signers cite unproven spying allegations tied to two affairs. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO; Harvey Jones chairs the board.
items.title: Campaign Pushes for Jensen Huang's Return as Nvidia CEO Amid Due-Process Demands

items.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said India and the US are near finalizing a trade pact begun in early 2025 to address tariffs, remove non-tariff barriers, and expand market access. He called it balanced and beneficial for both nations, noting the US is India's largest economy and biggest market.
items.title: India-US Trade Deal Nears Completion as Negotiations Approach Finishing Line

items.summary: Canadian PM Mark Carney announced a sweeping free-trade pact with the Philippines, expected to be signed within six months and dropping over 90% of tariff lines. Total trade reached about $2.4 billion in 2025, projected to triple by 2035. A broader ASEAN agreement is also nearly concluded. Carney frames these deals as reducing reliance on the United States amid ongoing US-Canada tensions.
items.title: Canada's Carney Promotes Philippine Trade Deal Amid US Diversification Push

items.summary: A senior Indian government official told news agency ANI that the US has assured India a comparative tariff advantage over competing economies under proposed bilateral trade negotiations, though the extent depends on the final structure. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal expressed confidence that India would secure one of its best deals with Washington, gaining preferred market access in products of interest. Negotiations proceed in phases, with services deferred to later stages; both sides finalized the first-phase framework in February amid shifting US tariffs.
items.title: US Assures India of Lower Tariffs Than Rival Economies in Trade Deal

items.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said India and the US have resolved most issues in their proposed trade deal, including tariff lines, with finalisation possible soon. He noted remaining concerns largely stem from the American side. Remarks precede PM Modi's likely December visit to Miami for the G20 Summit.
items.title: India-US Trade Deal Nears Finalisation as Negotiations Reach Finishing Line

items.summary: At their first trade council meeting on Nov 13, China and the United States held candid exchanges on tariffs, a reciprocal $30 billion-for-$30 billion tariff-cut arrangement, agricultural trade and other mutual concerns. Neither side confirmed whether agreements were reached, though both pledged to continue using the council to expand cooperation and reduce outstanding issues ahead of an expected leaders' meeting in Shenzhen next week.
items.title: China and US Open First Trade Council Meeting on Tariffs and Farm Goods

items.summary: The coming week is expected to open stable to cautiously positive, with the Nifty facing resistance at 25,425 and 25,550. Weekly technicals remain bullish—the RSI sits at 61.71 above neutral, MACD stays above its signal line—and the index has recovered above its 50-week (24,259) and 100-week (24,321) moving averages, with support below at 24,850 and 24,600. The recovery structure holds as long as Nifty stays within the 24,250–24,320 zone.
items.title: Dalal Street Week Ahead: Nifty Bulls Face Key Resistance Levels

items.summary: The Kerala High Court has suggested reducing the legal age threshold for juveniles from 18 to 16, arguing that children today demonstrate sufficient maturity by age 16. The court's reasoning reflects observed shifts in developmental readiness among younger populations. This proposal would redefine who qualifies as a juvenile under applicable law and could affect sentencing and protection frameworks nationwide.
items.title: Kerala High Court Proposes Lowering Juvenile Age Threshold to 16

items.summary: India's External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar stated at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit that bilateral trade negotiations with the US are in their final stretch, having begun last year after Trump-era tariffs of 50% were imposed on Indian exports. Talks accelerated following an earlier agreement to reduce rates to 18%, though he declined a timeline and emphasized India seeks a balanced deal granting comparative advantage over comparable economies. Jaishankar noted bipartisan US support for defence cooperation but warned the Democratic mid-term gains could alter relations, while addressing China's economic overtaking since the late 1980s and infrastructure hardening along the Line of Actual Control following the June 2020 Galwan clash.
items.title: Jaishankar Signals India-US Trade Deal Near Completion Amid China and Domestic Challenges

items.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said on Saturday that India and the US have resolved the bulk of issues in their proposed trade deal, including tariff lines, with hopes it could be sealed soon. He noted many remaining concerns are not at India's end but reflect changes made more by Washington. Negotiations began in early 2025 to address tariff friction, remove non-tariff barriers and expand market access. Jaishankar emphasized the deal should benefit both nations—India gaining better tariffs for its goods while benefiting from ties with America's largest economy—and stressed it requires patient, line-by-line work rather than quick resolution.
items.title: India-US Trade Deal Nears Final Breakthrough As EAM S Jaishankar Says Bulk Of Issues Resolved

items.summary: As artificial intelligence evolves rapidly, balancing innovation with risk control has become a shared priority across APEC economies. Shenzhen has rolled out pioneering local pilot programs covering AI legislation, algorithm filing and ethical review, exploring replicable "agile governance" pathways for the region. CGTN interviewed six tech enterprises based in Futian Industrial parks to capture frontline perspectives spanning judicial AI, life-science research, healthcare, rail infrastructure, digital solutions and cybersecurity, demonstrating how customized large-model applications meet diverse needs rather than relying on one-size-fits-all systems.
items.title: Shenzhen's Approach to AI Governance in the Asia-Pacific

items.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said on Saturday that India and the US have sorted out most issues relating to a proposed trade deal, which could be sealed "soon." Speaking at the HT Leadership Summit, he noted negotiations are near the "finishing line," with many remaining concerns not so much at India's end as on the American side. Talks began in early 2025 to address tariff friction and boost market access. Jaishankar emphasized the deal should be balanced and beneficial, noting the US is India's biggest market. Speculation exists that a Modi-Trump meeting during the December 14-15 G20 Summit in Miami could precede an announcement.
items.title: India-US Trade Deal May Seal 'Soon,' Final Hurdles Remain: Jaishankar

items.summary: The FAA lifted a nationwide ground stop Friday evening after hours of disruption affected thousands of flights, with cancellations and delays expected to continue through the weekend. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed the country's aging air traffic control system as "incredibly old" and requested $50 billion in emergency funding for its overhaul. The stop was the first since January 2023 and the second since September 11, 2001.
items.title: FAA Lifts Nationwide Ground Stop After Thousands of Flights Disrupted

items.summary: The UK is expected to have a milder weekend as an unusual autumn freeze eases off, following cold health alerts and overnight temperature drops. Most areas should enjoy fine, sunny weather Saturday morning after frost, though torrential rain and strong winds will hit the north and far west, with snow possible in north-west Scotland. Temperatures ranged from 5C to 11C on Saturday morning, having fallen as low as -6.6C overnight.
items.title: Milder Weekend Forecast in UK as Autumn Freeze Eases Off

items.summary: Shenzhen, the Chinese tech hub hosting APEC this week, shows food deliveries across its skies as a regular sight in busy tourist areas. The city illustrates how drones are easing life for delivery drivers and hungry visitors on the move. China has emerged as one of the world's most advanced markets for commercial drone logistics.
items.title: China's Drone Economy Delivers Big in Shenzhen

items.summary: A new book by a pair of economists argues that in-person collaboration boosts creativity and productivity. However, they caution that simply ordering workers back to the office is insufficient; employers must do more than mandate attendance to capture these benefits.
items.title: Economists Argue Office Mandates Fall Short of In-Person Creativity Benefits

items.summary: Italy's data protection agency fined Meta Platforms €805 million ($887 million) for accessing Android users' photos and videos without consent through a Facebook app feature. The fine equals about 0.47% of global revenue, with Meta given 60 days to disable the feature by default.
items.title: Italy Fines Meta $887 Million Over Android Users' Data Access

items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the United States raised whether Ukraine could join NATO in exchange for withdrawing from eastern Donbas. He would submit any proposal offering security guarantees, no military limits and rebuild funds to a referendum. Russia still demands territory and neutrality; Moscow occupies about a fifth of Ukrainian land. Relations between Kyiv and Washington remain strained over strikes on Russian oil facilities.
items.title: Zelensky says US floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for NATO membership

items.summary: Ransomware attacks have surged in recent months as cybercriminals combine established methods with new techniques enabled by artificial intelligence, according to cybersecurity researchers. While exact figures are hard to pin down because victims often don't disclose incidents and attackers inflate claims, some put alleged ransomware attacks on leak sites at nearly 3,000 over the summer—a 20 to 40 percent increase since spring. Cynthia Kaiser of Halcyon notes most recent increases stem from international attacks rather than steady U.S. activity. Allan Liska of Recorded Future says AI is increasingly used for phishing and negotiation, though successful groups remain largely human-operated. New ransomware groups like Global Secret Group and Storm have emerged rapidly, with one teenager reportedly earning over $800,000 in two weeks.
items.title: Beware the New AI-Fueled Ransomware Boom

items.summary: A cruise ship, the American Heritage, overturned after colliding with a tanker while docked in New Orleans, Louisiana on Friday. About 130 people were rescued from the vessel as it took on water. The incident left 32 people hospitalized with non-critical injuries. Mayor Helena Moreno called the situation "a miracle on the Mississippi," noting zero unaccounted-for individuals. The cause remains under investigation, with a possible steering fault suspected.
items.title: Cruise Ship Overturns After Collision With Tanker in New Orleans

items.summary: Dr. Siddhartha Mukherjee, oncologist and CEO of Manas AI, says artificial intelligence is shrinking early-stage cancer drug discovery from nearly eight years to three or four months at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit 2026 in New Delhi. His company's algorithms locate weak spots on disease-causing proteins—tasks that once took a decade now take just two hours—and pair with robotic testing for design-and-test cycles of three weeks, yielding candidates up to 200 times stronger than competitors. Mukherjee cautions cancer cannot be cured at once because each type is biologically distinct; pancreatic and stomach cancers remain hard challenges.
items.title: AI Compresses Early-Stage Cancer Drug Discovery From Years To Months

items.summary: In Shenzhen, China, anyone with a tech idea can design an electronic and have it produced within 20 minutes. CGTN's Toni Waterman visited the city while covering APEC to customize her own AI companion in one of the world's largest electronics hubs.
items.title: In Shenzhen, you can make your own electronic in 20 min

items.summary: On Friday, November 13, the FAA grounded flights nationwide for over four hours—the first such ground stop since January 2023 and only the second since September 11, 2001. Trump administration officials attributed the disruption to new technology overwhelming outdated air traffic control equipment, causing communication failures and radar gaps. The CNN report claimed more than 15,000 flights were disrupted through cancellations and delays.
items.title: US Airlines Face Longest Nationwide Ground Stop in 25 Years

items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said US peace envoys asked whether Kyiv would withdraw from Donbas in exchange for NATO membership, a prospect he noted had never been raised before. Reaffirming that Ukraine is not willing to cede territory, Zelenskyy added that if a comprehensive deal including security guarantees and reconstruction funds were reached, he would put the question to the public via referendum.
items.title: Zelenskyy Says Security Deal Could Go to Referendum

items.summary: Three young people describe feeling excluded from the job market despite strong qualifications and effort. Aamir, 25, has applied for more than 1,000 jobs since graduating but remains on universal credit in east London. Alice, 24, a Oxford and Cambridge graduate living in Bristol, submitted 50 tailored applications after six months of hospitality work. Liam, 20, from Exeter, volunteers at community gardens while seeking roles that demand experience he cannot yet provide. Peter, 21, earned top grades but faces fierce national competition for software engineering jobs, citing AI as reducing the need for graduates and no local opportunities in Maidstone. All report demoralisation, ghosting and repeated rejection.
items.title: Young Graduates Feel Shut Out of Entry-Level Careers

items.summary: The Guardian launches a series chronicling eight young people struggling to enter work, set against warnings of Britain creating a 'lost generation.' Andy Burnham's government aims to reduce 16-24-year-olds not in education, employment or training (Neet), which has reached its highest level in a decade. Series participants range from age 20 to 26. Milburn estimates the youth jobs crisis costs £125bn annually, while those who reach 24 without ever working may lose up to £300,000 over their lifetimes. Many face rejection and ghosting, with mental health tolls and guilt about living at home recurring themes.
items.title: Guardian Series on Young Jobseekers Amid Youth Jobs Crisis

items.summary: Former wildland firefighter and union leader Sam Forstag defeated Republican Aaron Flint in Montana's 1st Congressional District, ending a three-decade absence of Democrats from the state's U.S. House delegation since Pat Williams retired in 1996. Forstag won with 132,003 votes (50.34%) versus Flint's 122,694 (46.79%), drawing strong support from Missoula County and Gallatin County to overcome rural losses. A former smokejumper who led the National Federation of Federal Employees, Forstag campaigned on wildfire preparedness, Forest Service staffing and protecting public lands, though he has not yet secured committee assignments or legislative wins despite reaching out to Republican colleagues.
items.title: Sam Forstag Ends Montana's Three-Decade Democratic House Absence

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV, the Chicago-born pontiff who holds Peruvian citizenship and is 71 years old, continues his tour of South America with masses drawing crowds of around 500,000 people. Health authorities across Latin America express heightened fears as measles cases surged to 57,666 confirmed in 17 countries from January to October, nearly five times the previous year, with at least 81 deaths reported. Low vaccination rates—90% and 82% for Peru's first and second doses versus 84% and 55% in Argentina—compound concerns, though only Uruguay met the 95% threshold.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV's South American Tour Amid Measles Concerns in Latin America

items.summary: Data-center growth and electrification are pushing Georgia Power toward a major grid expansion of between 2,000 and 6,000 megawatts for 2032-2033. The plan hinges on Effective Load Carrying Capability (ELCC), which measures how reliably each resource counts toward capacity: natural gas at roughly 60 to 80 percent versus solar or wind at just 4 to 40 percent without storage, but around 95 percent with batteries. Georgia Power now assigns battery storage only a 20 percent ELCC in its latest procurement—down from prior figures of up to 95 percent—so a 1,000-megawatt battery project counts for just 200 megawatts versus 800 for gas. Bob Sherrier of the Southern Environmental Law Center and Advanced Power Alliance calls this “a thumb on the scale for gas,” warning it could lock in millions more tons of annual emissions as renewables become less competitive.
items.title: Georgia Power's Lower Battery ELCC Favors Natural Gas in Grid Expansion

items.summary: Against a backdrop of prolonged conflicts, stretched supply chains, and weakened global institutions like the UN, WTO, G20, and US leadership under President Donald Trump, the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad) faces scrutiny. The November 17, 2026 summit in Manila will be its first leaders' meeting since September 2024 and the first held outside a Quad country. Originating from the December 2004 tsunami relief effort and revived amid China's rise, the grouping now must decide whether to remain an informal forum or become an actionable platform for maritime security, economic resilience, and Indo-Pacific stability.
items.title: Quad at a Crossroads: Can the Manila Summit Rediscover Its Purpose?

items.summary: Yes Bank has petitioned the Supreme Court to review an October 15 order upholding a Bombay High Court ruling that quashed its decision to write off Additional Tier 1 bonds. The high court found the administrator lacked authority and stayed its order for six weeks, allowing appeal.
items.title: Yes Bank Petitions Supreme Court Review of AT-1 Bond Write-off Quashing

items.summary: NASA reports that Voyager 1, launched in 1977 and now the most distant human-made object, is about to reach one light-day—roughly 16 billion miles (26 billion km) from Earth—at 5:16 a.m. ET on Wednesday. Astrophysicist Alan Cummings of Caltech calls it an engineering milestone that also demonstrates communication across such distance. The probe crossed the heliosphere in 2012 and entered interstellar space, while its twin Voyager 2 is projected to reach one light-day around November 2035.
items.title: NASA's Voyager 1 Approaches a Light-Day Milestone from Earth

items.summary: The article examines the accelerating integration of AI into aviation, contrasting Silicon Valley speed with air travel's conservative norms. It opens with FAA administrator Bryan Bedford touting SMART—an AI tool to cut delays—despite doubts about its reliability after a September groundstop that disrupted flights worldwide. Joby Aviation demonstrated pilotless eVTOL flight across 3,200 miles in California and Texas under the Trump administration's eIPP program. The piece traces drone delivery milestones: Google's Project Wing reached 164 homes near Canberra by 2018; Amazon plans to expand to 500 locations this year, while Walmart targets 270 stores by 2027.
items.title: AI's Rapid Inroads Into Aviation Amid Safety and Reliability Concerns

items.summary: The resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is framed as a major setback for the US open-model ecosystem, which had relied on his funding and crisis-management authority. Analysts argue that while open models have correctly targeted enterprise post-training and 'ownership of intelligence,' their long-term benefit remains unrealized amid scarce compute and fierce competition from closed labs like Anthropic with superior scale. Talent is concentrated at a few top firms rather than distributed, making it hard to simply fund an alternative to Chinese frontier models like Kimi or DeepSeek. Compounding concerns are rising state-level AI regulation driven by safety narratives, prompting calls to incubate a truly frontier US open-model player.
items.title: Open-source AI without Jensen

items.summary: Rampurhat Municipality in West Bengal's Birbhum district directed meat shops to remain closed for two days, Sunday and Monday, ahead of Chhath Puja. Municipal Chairman Soumen Bhagat said the order stemmed from festival arrangements and cited concerns that blood and water could spill onto roads, disturbing devotees' religious sentiments; he consulted the SDO and police IC before acting. The Bengal Congress rejected the directive as politically motivated, alleging it diverted attention from a recent police firing in the area and harmed traders' livelihoods.
items.title: Meat shops ordered to close during Chhath in Bengal's Birbhum; Congress slams move

items.summary: On his 78th birthday, King Charles joined Sir Elton John for a special episode of the singer's Rocket Hour radio show to celebrate 50 years of The King's Trust. Both joked they were "still standing" — though Elton noted he was sitting and both have health challenges. The charity has supported over one million young people since its launch.
items.title: King Charles Jokes 'Still Standing' With Elton John on Birthday Radio Show

items.summary: On Saturday, Türkiye joined 17 other nations in condemning an Israeli airstrike on the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis that injured patients and staff. The joint statement declared the attack a violation of international humanitarian law protecting medical facilities. Ministers condemned continued strikes on displaced civilians, warned worsening conditions as winter approaches threaten children and infants from exposure, and urged Israel to uphold the ceasefire under the Sharm El-Sheikh Agreement while allowing unimpeded humanitarian aid.
items.title: Türkiye and 17 Countries Condemn Israeli Gaza Hospital Strike; Demand Ceasefire Compliance
